evidence: Inspected the supplied unified diffs for bin/labdrian-overlay (resolve_latest_release_tag's new do_fetch parameter and fetch-guard) and tui/release_backend_test.go (updated and new tests). Both default-value parameter expansions and the bracket-test comparison are quoted, non-eval, and not subject to word-splitting or shell injection.

cmd_sync_check's release_version resolution now narrows rather than expands network access; the code comment states the other four call sites (cmd_apply, cmd_self_update, cmd_update, cmd_version) are unmodified and remain on the do_fetch=true default, and no call site bypasses the new gate for cmd_sync_check's default path.
No command injection, unsafe/unquoted variable expansion, privilege escalation, secret exposure, or dependency-vulnerability evidence was found.
openspec/changes/overlay-versioned-releases/verify-report.md is unchanged since its independent approval under prior lineage review-270a5e0f9b44565b; no new content was inspected there.

The new TestReleaseBackend_SyncCheck_DefaultDoesNotFetchTags differentially proves, via git tag -l staying empty, exit code 0, and the ACTION-line text, that the flagless default sync-check path performs zero git fetch and degrades gracefully to the untagged/apply-recommendation fallback rather than crashing or fabricating a release version.

The default parameter value ('true') on resolve_latest_release_tag's new do_fetch parameter structurally reproduces the exact prior always-fetch condition for every untouched call site (cmd_apply, cmd_self_update, cmd_update, cmd_version), so the behavior change is provably scoped to cmd_sync_check only.
TestReleaseBackend_SyncCheck_DigestMismatchActionNamesReleaseVersion was updated to pass --fetch, preserving its original always-fetch scenario without weakening its assertions.

No regression, missing-fallback, or blast-radius defect is evidenced. openspec/changes/overlay-versioned-releases/verify-report.md carried no diff in this context and was triaged as covered per its prior review-reliability approval under lineage review-270a5e0f9b44565b.

resolve_latest_release_tag's doc-comment was updated to '<ref> [do_fetch=true]', matching its actual implementation default, so the new parameter's name, optionality, and default are unambiguous from the signature alone.

The accompanying prose explicitly names every caller (cmd_apply, cmd_self_update, cmd_update, cmd_version) that keeps the do_fetch=true default and explains why only cmd_sync_check's read-only default path needs do_fetch=false, tying the rationale to concrete requirement IDs (sync-check-verdicts R-001, tui-self-update R-001).

The new TestReleaseBackend_SyncCheck_DefaultDoesNotFetchTags has a self-describing name and a comment naming the exact regression (sdd-verify CRITICAL-1), the violated requirements, the reproduction scenario, and the specific TUI call path (probeBehindOriginCmd) that depends on the fix; its assertions directly match the stated intent.

No misleading names, duplicated/dead logic, unexplained constants, unsafe complexity, or missing change context was found. openspec/changes/overlay-versioned-releases/verify-report.md is unchanged since its prior review-reliability approval and is reported as covered.

findings.claim: resolve_latest_release_tag's new do_fetch parameter defaults via bash's ${2:-true} expansion, which substitutes the default for both an unset AND an empty-string second argument; if cmd_sync_check's check_origin variable could ever be empty rather than the literal string 'false', the default sync-check path would still resolve do_fetch to true and keep fetching.
proof_refs: bin/labdrian-overlay:459 (new line): local do_fetch="${2:-true}" -- POSIX/bash ${var:-default} parameter expansion applies the default when the parameter is unset OR null (empty).

bin/labdrian-overlay:1848: local check_origin=false -- check_origin is always initialized to the literal string 'false' (never empty) and only ever reassigned the literal string 'true' by the --check-origin/--fetch flag branch, so this hypothetical does not manifest in the shipped code.

evidence: Confirmed the new test drives real git plumbing (newScratchRepo, pushUpstreamTag, runGit against actual temporary repositories) rather than a mock, and asserts both the absence of fetched tags after a flagless sync-check and the absence of a named release version in its untagged-fallback ACTION line -- reproducing the exact CRITICAL-1 scenario.

Confirmed TestReleaseBackend_SyncCheck_DigestMismatchActionNamesReleaseVersion's original digest-mismatch/ACTION-naming assertions are unaffected by the added --fetch flag, since --fetch only re-establishes the pre-fix precondition (a resolvable release version) that the candidate's new default path no longer provides implicitly.

Verified against the full (non-diff-scoped) source: cmd_sync_check's check_origin local is declared 'local check_origin=false' (bin/labdrian-overlay:1848) and only ever reassigned the literal string 'true' on --check-origin/--fetch -- never an empty string -- so the WARNING finding below (raised from diff-only evidence that could not see this declaration) does not manifest in the shipped code; recorded as WARNING/informational rather than a corrected defect.

openspec/changes/overlay-versioned-releases/verify-report.md carried no patch in this context; per the supplied note it is unchanged since its prior independent review-reliability approval under lineage review-270a5e0f9b44565b, so it is listed as covered with no re-inspection performed for new findings.
